parsed.explanation: The objection is locally right that writing $P_{\mathrm{final}}$ presupposes the play ends. But the same sentence supplies the prefix version: "Since $P$ is always a positive integer and each type A move at least halves it" — 'always' quantifies over every reachable position, so after any $t$ type A moves the current product satisfies $1 \le P \le P_0/2^t$, forcing $t \le \lfloor\log_2 P_0\rfloor$. Combined with the independently proved bound of at most $N$ type B moves (from $z$ non-decreasing, bounded by $N$, increasing at each type B move), no infinite play exists. Only the label $P_{\mathrm{final}}$ needs changing to the current $P$; the termination argument itself is complete for every play.
